newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian airline hopes to restructure its debts.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian airline hopes to restructure its debts.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-run Balkan Airlines plans to stabilise its finances by restructuring its debt before the firm is offered for sale, Executive Director Valeri Doganov said on Monday.
Doganov told a news conference a debt restructuring could be the first step towards Balkan's planned privatisation and would make it more attractive for potential investors.
He said Balkan could buy the foreign debt of local banks which have been placed in receivership on the international secondary debt market, enabling it to repay its debt to those banks at a discount.
He said another option was to offer Balkan's domestic creditors the option of buying shares.
"It is also possible that a stable financial institution buys the debt which the airline owes to Bulgarian banks against its participation in the airline's capital when it is privatised," he said.

He declined to specify the size of Balkan's debt but said the airline owed sums to Bulgarian banks and firms for supplies of petroleum products, to Bulstrad insurance company, Sofia airport and air traffic controllers.
Balkan's foreign debts include debts to firms for fuel supplies and unpaid taxes for flights over other countries.

Balkan, which incurred losses of $50 million last year due to leasing fees, the drastic fall of the lev to the dollar and penalties on overdue payments, has returned all its four Airbus A320s leased from Japanese firm Orix Corp.
Two Airbuses were detained in London and Amsterdam for unpaid fees last December.
Doganov said the company had started operating under a stabilisation programme and had reduced its losses by $700,000 for the first two months of the year against the same period last year.
"We will revise all the deals Balkan has recently sealed but it is not easy to cancel those which are unfavourable for the company," Doganov said.
Bulgaria began moves to privatise the national carrier in 1992, but in January 1995 the Privatisation Agency suspended the plan, citing a lack of buyers.
Balkan needs finances to buy new planes and replace its old Soviet-made aircraft, officials said. The airline has 18 Tupolev TU-154s, two Ilyushin IL-18s, four Antonov AN-12s and six AN-24s.
The airline has two Boeing 767-200s leased from Air France and three Boeing 737-500s leased from Australia's Ansett.
Doganov said the Privatisation Agency had blocked Balkan's sale of its Pliska hotel in Sofia at the behest of Bulgaria's Economic Bank as Balkan owes the bank $11 million.
